pages.title: TASKS
pages.text:
ROT DEFORMATION

A plant may be sick if you observe:

spots on the leaves (black, white, or brown), signs of rot on the fruits or roots,

- deformed or curled leaves, permanent wilting, even if the plant has received enough water.

WILTING
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour TÂCHES

pages.title: TOO MUCH WATER
pages.text:
TOO DRY TOO HOT/COLD TOO CROWDED

Diseases develop if:

- **Too much water**: overly frequent watering, constantly wet soil, prolonged rain.

- **Not enough water**: a thirsty plant is less resistant to diseases.

- **Intense heat or cold snap**: sudden variations can weaken the plant and activate diseases.

- **Lack of air between plants**: overly crowded spacing promotes stagnant humidity and thus diseases.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour TROP D’EAU

pages.title: CUT
pages.text:
REMOVE STRENGTHEN TREAT What to do when a plant is sick?

- Eliminate affected parts: cut off diseased leaves, stems, or fruits to prevent spread.

- Remove the entire plant if it is too sick and cannot be saved.

- Strengthen the plant and soil with a light application of compost or compost tea.

- Apply a natural treatment: garlic infusion, neem slurry, baking soda…
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour COUPER

pages.title: THINNING THE FOLIAGE
pages.text:
ADAPT WATERING +

To prevent the disease from returning, you can:

- Thin the foliage to allow air and light to pass through, and limit stagnant humidity.

- Adapt watering
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour ÉCLAIRCIR LE FEUILLAGE

pages.title: Yellow Leaves
pages.text:
Deformed fruits
Slow growth
Purple stems
Dry edges
When a plant doesn't receive all the nutrients it needs, it shows.

A plant may be deficient if you observe:

- Yellow leaves (often at the bottom)
- Small or deformed fruits
- Red or purple stems
- Leaves with dry, red, or purple edges
- Slow growth, stunted plants
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Feuilles jaunes

pages.title: POOR SOIL
pages.text:
COMPACT SOIL UNBALANCED PH

Deficiencies appear when:

- The soil is poor and compost is absent or of poor quality.

- The soil is too compact or poorly aerated: water and nutrients cannot properly reach the roots.

- The soil's pH (acidity or basicity) is unbalanced: too acidic or too basic, it can block certain nutrients, even if they are present in the soil.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour SOL PAUVRE

pages.title: STRENGTHEN
pages.text:
TREAT TEST BASIC U IDE AC pH IDE AC BASIC NEUTRAL pH NEUTRAL E ANALYZE

To correct a deficiency, one can:

- Add mature compost regularly: 1 to 2 wheelbarrows per bed depending on the crop
- Use leaf manure (nettle, comfrey, neem, etc.) to stimulate growth
- Test the soil pH if the problem persists (pH paper or simple kit). If it is too acidic, it can be corrected with a small amount of agricultural lime.

- Perform a soil analysis to provide missing elements
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour RENFORCER

pages.title: Visible Insects
pages.text:
Eggs Deformed or sticky leaves Damaged fruits Galleries

Pest insects weaken plants, reduce harvests, and transmit diseases. It's best to spot them early to limit damage:

- **Visible insects**: caterpillars, whiteflies, aphids, locusts, maggots…
- **Holes in leaves**: eaten edges or round holes in the center
- **Pierced, rotten, or gnawed fruits** before maturity
- **Deformed or sticky leaves**: presence of aphids
- **Small galleries** in leaves or roots: worms, nematodes
- **Presence of eggs** on stems or under leaves
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Insectes visibles

pages.title: MONITOR CLOSELY:
pages.text:
Young seedlings Stressed plants

- Cabbage, tomato, bean, and okra crops

Certain plants are more vulnerable and must be monitored closely:

Young seedlings and transplants, with tender leaves very attractive to insects
Stressed or weakened plants, which defend themselves less effectively
Crops like cabbage, tomatoes, beans, or okra are more frequently attacked
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour SURVEILLER DE PRÈS :

pages.title: CUT
pages.text:
SPRAY

If you have spotted signs of pests:

- Remove heavily infested leaves to slow down the infestation
- Spray plants to dislodge harmful insects
- Install fine nets or screens against flying insects
PROTECT
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour COUPER

pages.title: MONITORING
pages.text:
PLANT REPELLENTS ATTRACT BENEFICIAL INSECTS BASIL MINT LEMONGRASS WASP LADYBUG

To prevent pests from returning:

- Regularly observe under the leaves and on young shoots. This allows early detection of problems.

- Plant repellent plants such as basil, mint, lemongrass, or marigolds next to your crops.

- Attract beneficial insects, like ladybugs or certain wasps, which eat pests. Place harmful insects on a plate near the crops with seeds to attract birds. They will then come and pick the harmful insects directly from the plants.

pages.title: The plant seems to be doing poorly, but no pests or diseases are visible. What if it's stress? This is visible through:
pages.text:
- It wilts in the middle of the day, especially during hot weather.

- It has stopped growing.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour La plante semble aller mal, mais aucun ravageur ni maladie n’est visible. Et si c’était du stress ? Cela est visible par :

pages.title: TOO HOT/COLD
pages.text:
TOO DRY/WET
POOR TRANSPLANTING IN FULL SUN
TOO EARLY/LATE

What causes stress in plants:

- Soil that is too hot or too cold
- Extreme variations: too dry, too wet
- Poor transplanting or transplanting in full sun
- Transplanting too early or too late
- Compact soil: roots struggle to establish themselves
COMPACT SOIL
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour TROP CHAUD/FROID

pages.title: MULCHING
pages.text:
WATER + PROTECT SHADE NET

Wait before treating: stress disappears in 1–2 days if the plant returns to good conditions. If stress persists:

- Mulch to retain soil moisture
- Water regularly without excess
- Protect plants with a shade cloth
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour PAILLER

pages.text:
VARIETIES RESPECTING DISTANCES How to plant well in bio-intensive? 

- Choose your varieties according to the seasons
- Respect planting distances
- Associate crops
- Practice crop rotations

ASSOCIATE CROPS PRACTICE ROTATIONS

pages.title: ADAPT
pages.text:
WATERING MULCH COMPOST + GENTLE IRRIGATION

How to maintain your crops in living soil:

- Regularly apply compost / compost tea
- Mulch abundantly
- Water beds and pathways with gentle irrigation
- Use insect netting
- Adapt water supply according to the plant's growth stage
NETTING

pages.title: With living, well-nourished soil, netting to protect crops, and appropriate natural treatments, we can prevent
pages.text:
and manage most problems without using chemical products.

By practicing good crop rotation and making intelligent variety choices, we also promote more resilient plants and better harvests.
